items.title: Monday's bounce fades in tech while Dow and most sectors hold — rotation, not full reversal
items.summary: After Monday's surge (S&P 500 +4.73% to 7,237.17 at the close), Tuesday is mixed: the Dow is higher while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are lower, with losses concentrated in technology and health care leading. The VIX spiked above 30 premarket, then eased back into the high 26s by early afternoon. Breadth outside tech is positive, so the session so far reads as a partial fade and rotation rather than a wholesale reversal.

items.title: Nvidia gives back about 7% intraday as Huang-return rally unwinds on political backlash; Dec 3 Senate testimony confirmed
items.summary: Nvidia fell 5.2% premarket and slid to about -7% intraday after closing Monday up 31.5% on Jensen Huang's reinstatement. Bipartisan opposition is confirmed: Sen. Warren called the reinstatement reckless and sought export-compliance information; Sen. Cotton renewed calls for the Chip Security Act. Huang's public Senate Banking Committee testimony on export controls is confirmed for Dec 3, with a closed House interview Dec 1. The reinstatement itself stands; the give-back reflects governance and export-control repricing, including Commerce blacklisting Megaspeed and related entities.

items.title: HPE beats and raises guidance on AI servers, but stock falls about 17% on margin outlook
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise's fiscal Q4 (reported Monday after the bell) confirmed revenue +50% to $14.55B, server revenue +94.7% to $8.8B, adjusted EPS $1.43 vs about $1.28 expected, and FY27 revenue guidance raised to $59.4-63.1B. The stock fell anyway — about -17% intraday — because FY27 Cloud & AI operating margin is guided down to about 14% from 18.4% in Q4, and management warned memory and component supply stays constrained into at least H2 2028. Part of the drop also gives back Monday's +17% rally.

items.title: Best Buy posts strongest comparable sales in five years and raises full-year guidance
items.summary: Best Buy's Q3 release (quarter ended Oct 31) confirms comparable sales +6.1% — the highest in five years, vs 2.3% consensus — revenue +5.8% to $10.24B, and adjusted EPS of $1.62. FY27 guidance was raised: revenue $43.0-43.3B, comparable sales +3.4-4.0%, adjusted EPS $6.90-7.05. Management attributed strength to AI-enabled phones and TVs, wearables and gaming ahead of the holidays — a genuine consumer-electronics demand signal.

items.title: Sanofi to acquire Insmed for $41B cash — largest pharma deal since 2023
items.summary: Sanofi announced Tuesday it will acquire Insmed for $175 per share in cash, about $41.0B equity value — a premium of about 17% to Monday's close and 46% to the Nov 18 unaffected price. Both boards approved; close is expected H1 2027. The deal brings Brinsupri and Arikayce and is Sanofi's largest in over two decades. Insmed rose about 14% to about $170 in early trade.

items.title: China extends critical-minerals export relief to Jan 27, 2027 — the Nov 27 cliff is off
items.summary: China's Commerce Ministry announced Tuesday it will extend the suspension of its ban on U.S.-bound dual-use exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials through Jan 27, 2027; the suspension had been due to expire Friday Nov 27. The ban on exports to U.S. military end-users remains in place, as do worldwide licensing requirements. The move follows the Nov 18-19 Xi-Trump meeting and aligns with the broader trade truce.

items.title: Pentagon in preliminary talks with GM, Ford and Magna on military drone production — no deals
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that the Pentagon is in preliminary talks with GM, Ford, Magna International and others to mass-produce military drones, with automakers supplying parts such as motors, actuators and sensors rather than building complete aircraft. No deals have been finalized. Reuters carried the story but noted it could not independently verify it, and no company has confirmed — this item is single-origin reporting and graded accordingly. GM and Ford shares showed no clear reaction attributable to the story.

items.title: Amazon signs Decart tech-and-team deal; reported $7.5B price is unconfirmed
items.summary: Amazon announced Monday a signed agreement to acquire the technology behind Decart's Optimization Stack and hire its three co-founders and research/engineering team. Amazon clarified it is an asset purchase, not a full company acquisition, and did not disclose a price. The approximately $7.5B figure comes from a single Bloomberg source and is not confirmed by either company — the deal's existence and structure are corroborated; the price is reported only.

observations.value: Signed agreement announced Nov 23 (Amazon blog post); asset purchase of Decart Optimization Stack technology plus team

observations.value: About $7.5B per a Bloomberg source; NOT confirmed by Amazon or Decart — treat as unverified

items.key_finding: Amazon-Decart is signed and real, but it is a tech-and-team asset purchase and the $7.5B headline number is single-source and unconfirmed.
